Entry Concept of Rule in Slaver's Bay The view of governance in Slaver's Bay is shaped by the ancient nobility, slavery, city walls, and the suppressed majority. It is not an abstract principle: a superior person uses it to explain why he should be obeyed, and a subordinate person tests this theory by whether he can get protection, food and justice. Whether it is valid depends on who can grant the rights, collect the consideration, and actually make the judgment come to fruition in the event of default.

Entry Concept of Rule in Slaver's Bay The view of governance in Slaver's Bay is shaped by the ancient nobility, slavery, city walls, and the suppressed majority. It is not an abstract principle: a superior person uses it to explain why he should be obeyed, and a subordinate person tests this theory by whether he can get protection, food and justice. If a rule is practiced over and over again, it will find its way into rituals, crafts, and prayers; if it is sustained only by fear, cracks will show at the onset of a crisis.
